title: Applications of Royen's Gaussian Correlation Inequality in high-dimensional testing
summary: Royen's Gaussian Correlation Inequality (GCI) is a fundamental result in statistics and probability, but unfortunately, at least by now, the result is not very well known in the statistical community. In this paper, we demonstrate the potential of GCI in high-dimensional testing problems that involve multivariate Gaussian variables. Leveraging the GCI, we establish sharp Type I error bounds under arbitrary Gaussian covariance structures.
